items.title: Section: Fewer and Fewer Faculties the Deeper Into Meditation One Goes, and Whether the Highest Absorption Is Truly Undefiled

items.zh: 第二靜慮地亦爾。問：第三靜慮地幾根可得？答：十七。問：第四靜慮地幾根可得？答：十六。問：空無邊處地幾根可得？答：十一。如空無邊處地，識無邊處地、無所有處地，應知亦爾。問：非想非非想處地幾根可得？答：八。問：初靜慮地所攝諸根，當言有漏？當言無漏？答：當言二種。如初靜慮所攝諸根，乃至無所有處地所攝諸根，當知亦爾。非想非非想處地所攝諸根，當言有漏。此約種類。若約相續，當言二種。又由煩惱解脫故，令彼諸根成無漏性。
items.en: The second absorption is likewise. Question: how many faculties are obtainable in the third absorption? Answer: seventeen. Question: in the fourth absorption? Answer: sixteen. Question: in the sphere of infinite space? Answer: eleven. As with the sphere of infinite space, so too should the spheres of infinite consciousness and nothingness be understood. Question: in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception? Answer: eight. Question: are the faculties subsumed under the first absorption defiled or undefiled? Answer: they should be said to be both. The faculties subsumed under the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception should be said to be defiled — this considered by type. Considered by the particular being involved, they should be said to be both, since through liberation from affliction those very faculties can become undefiled in nature.

items.zh: 如有漏無漏，如是應斷不應斷、世間出世間，當知亦爾。

items.title: Section: What a Hell-Being Still Possesses, and What Depends on Having the Seed of Liberation at All

items.zh: 問：若生欲界，當言成就幾根？答：容有一切。問：生那落迦成就幾根？答：八，現行、種子皆得成就。除三，所餘或成就、或不成就。三，約現行不成就，約種子或成就，謂般涅槃法；或不成就，謂不般涅槃法。餘三，現行故不成就，種子故成就。
items.en: Question: for one born in the desire realm, how many faculties should be said to be possessed? Answer: potentially all of them. Question: for one born in the hells, how many are possessed? Answer: eight, possessed both as active manifestation and as seed. Excepting three, the remaining faculties may or may not be possessed.

items.title: Section: Pampered Dogs, Suffering Ghosts, and Why Humans Can Possess Every Single Faculty

items.zh: 如生那落迦趣，於一向苦傍生、餓鬼，當知亦爾。若苦樂雜受處，後三種亦現行成就。問：若生人趣成就幾根？答：容有一切。如生人中，生天亦爾。
items.en: As with rebirth in the hells, so too should it be understood for animals and hungry ghosts whose existence is one of unrelieved suffering. Where pleasure and pain are experienced together, the latter three faculties can also manifest actively. Question: for one reborn as a human, how many faculties should be said to be possessed? Answer: potentially all of them. As with rebirth among humans, so too for rebirth among the gods.

items.title: Section: Missing Faculties, Severed Roots, and the Line Between Ordinary Beings and Those Who Have Seen the Truth

items.zh: 問：諸缺根者成就幾根？答：除五，容有餘。問：諸具根者成就幾根？答：容有一切。問：諸半擇迦成就幾根？答：除五，容有餘。問：女成就幾根？答：容有二十一。問：男成就幾根？答：亦容有二十一。問：諸二形者成就幾根？答：容有十九。問：斷善根者成就幾根？答：除八，容有餘。問：不斷善根者成就幾根？答：容有一切。問：諸異生成就幾根？答：十九，除後三。問：諸見諦者成就幾根？答：容有一切。
items.en: Question: for those lacking a faculty, how many can be possessed? Answer: excepting five, potentially the rest. Question: for those with complete faculties? Answer: potentially all. Question: for eunuchs? Answer: excepting five, potentially the rest. Question: for a woman? Answer: potentially twenty-one. Question: for a man? Answer: likewise potentially twenty-one. Question: for a hermaphrodite? Answer: potentially nineteen. Question: for one who has severed wholesome roots? Answer: excepting eight, potentially the rest. Question: for one who has not severed wholesome roots? Answer: potentially all. Question: for an ordinary being? Answer: nineteen, excepting the final three. Question: for one who has seen the truth? Answer: potentially all.

items.title: Section: Counting Down the Faculties Stage by Stage, from Stream-Entry to Arhatship

items.zh: 問：有學成就幾根？答：容有二十一。問：無學成就幾根？答：容有十九。問：預流果向成就幾根？答：容有二十。問：預流果成就幾根？答：亦容有二十。如預流果，一來果向、一來果、不還果向，當知亦爾。問：不還果成就幾根？答：容有十九。如不還果，阿羅漢向亦爾。問：阿羅漢果成就幾根？答：容有十九。問：若生色界成就幾根？答：容有十八。問：生無色界成就幾根？答：容有十一。
items.en: Question: how many can a trainee possess? Answer: potentially twenty-one. Question: how many can one beyond training possess? Answer: potentially nineteen. Question: how many can one approaching stream-entry possess? Answer: potentially twenty. Question: how many can one who has attained the fruit of stream-entry possess? Answer: likewise potentially twenty. As with the fruit of stream-entry, so too should the approach to once-returning, the fruit of once-returning, and the approach to non-returning be understood. Question: how many can one who has attained the fruit of non-returning possess? Answer: potentially nineteen. As with the fruit of non-returning, so too the approach to arhatship. Question: how many can one who has attained the fruit of arhatship possess? Answer: potentially nineteen. Question: how many can one reborn in the form realm possess? Answer: potentially eighteen. Question: how many can one reborn in the formless realm possess? Answer: potentially eleven.

items.title: Section: Four Ways to Lose or Gain a Faculty Between One Life and the Next

items.zh: 問：若欲界沒欲界生時，當言捨幾根，得幾根？答：且約色根容有而說。或捨缺諸根，得缺諸根；或捨缺諸根，得具諸根；或捨具諸根，得具諸根；或捨具諸根，得缺諸根。或捨劣諸根，得劣諸根；或捨劣諸根，得勝諸根；或捨勝諸根，得劣諸根；或捨勝諸根，得勝諸根。
items.en: Question: for one who dies in the desire realm and is reborn there, how many faculties should be said to be relinquished, and how many obtained? Answer: considering the physical faculties as an example: one may relinquish deficient faculties and obtain deficient faculties; relinquish deficient faculties and obtain complete faculties; relinquish complete faculties and obtain complete faculties; or relinquish complete faculties and obtain deficient faculties. One may relinquish inferior faculties and obtain inferior faculties; relinquish inferior faculties and obtain superior faculties; relinquish superior faculties and obtain inferior faculties; or relinquish superior faculties and obtain superior faculties.

items.zh: 意根、命根勝劣得捨，當知亦爾。若諸受根勝劣得捨，隨其所應亦爾。此約異熟果故有差別。若諸善根約等流果，捨前前劣，得後後勝，非由生故。捨勝得劣，後邪方便乃有斯義。最後三根，於一切位與生相違，是故不說。問：從欲界沒色界生時，捨幾根，得幾根？答：容捨下地一切，容得上地一切。如欲界沒色界生時，從欲界沒無色生時，從色界沒無色生時，當知亦爾。

items.title: Section: A Summary Verse Closes Eight Distinctions, and a Second, Even Longer List Begins

items.zh: 最後三根，由證沙門果方便而得，不由沒生。先修習力所任持故，後等流果轉盛而生。又能為緣，生異熟果，令轉明盛。中嗢拕南曰：業實有、色等、善等、異熟等、若界、若諸地、及死生得捨。問：幾根由境界義名有義？幾非耶？答：二十一名有義，一非。
items.en: The final three faculties are obtained through the means of realising a contemplative's fruit, not through death and rebirth. Because of the sustaining power of prior cultivation, the equal-outflow result that follows grows ever more vigorous. They also serve as a condition generating a karmic-ripening result, causing it to grow ever brighter. The middle summary verse states: function, real existence, form and the rest, moral quality and karmic ripening, realm and meditative stage, and death-and-rebirth's obtaining and relinquishing. Question: how many faculties possess the meaning of an object? How many do not? Answer: twenty-one possess it; one does not.

blocks.text: How many faculties a being has depends on where and what they are: in hell, among humans, at each stage of the path.

Master Cháng Bǎi: at the peak of existence only eight faculties remain, without the three uncontaminated ones, since that absorption is too dim for the path. (Untranslated, 0615a07: the stage before the first meditation has eleven faculties; why joy there is not counted as in the first meditation: it is still unsteady. The first meditation has eighteen.)
Eight, as manifestation and as seed. Master Cháng Bǎi: because evil karma makes the five sense doors suffer constantly, the five faculties are surely complete.
One who has severed wholesome roots lacks eight; an ordinary being has nineteen, without the final three. Master Cháng Bǎi: one who has severed roots still has them as potential.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the non-returner has cut all desire-realm desire and so has no sorrow.

Four cases of deficient and complete, inferior and superior physical faculties. (Untranslated, 0615c01: wholesome faculties improve through outflow results, the better replacing the worse; leaving the desire realm for the form realm, one may give up all the lower faculties and gain all the higher.)
Twenty-one faculties have objects; one does not. Master Cháng Bǎi: the life faculty has no object; it is drawn by past karma.
"Humans can possess every faculty." This is why a human birth is called precious: it is the only birth with the whole set.

quiz.q: The English has "by type" and "by the particular being involved." How is this, and why are the peak sphere's faculties contaminated?
options: poor: 種類 means race and 相續 family; all beings there are noble, so all are uncontaminated
poor: both should be "type"
poor: that stage has no faculties
good: the Sub-commentary reads by stage and by person; that stage is too dim for the path, so by stage contaminated, by a liberated person uncontaminated
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in the peak sphere only eight faculties can be found, without the three uncontaminated, since that absorption is dim and the path cannot be cultivated there; by the difference of realm and stage, this is by type. The English "by the particular being involved" fits the Sub-commentary's reading, and a liberated person's faculties there can be uncontaminated.

quiz.q: How many faculties does one born in the hells possess, and why are the five complete?
options: all twenty-two manifest, hell-beings being just like humans and differing only in surroundings, so every faculty, the three uncontaminated included, can be active there
eight, as manifestation and seed; evil karma makes the five doors suffer always, and life is needed to receive it
only three: pain, sorrow, life
none at all
quiz.why: The treatise says eight, both as manifestation and as seed. Master Cháng Bǎi: because evil karma makes the five doors suffer constantly, the five faculties are surely complete; only with life can suffering be received; and in hell practice is impossible, so the three uncontaminated faculties cannot manifest.

quiz.q: Why do those lacking a faculty and hermaphrodites lack the three uncontaminated faculties?
options: because they have become arhats, transcending the three, as the treatise means
because they are all hell-beings
the lecturer says those without male or female faculties cannot train in the path, nor can hermaphrodites, and so they lack the three
because they have severed the life faculty
quiz.why: The treatise gives the counts; the explanation is the lecturer's: those without male or female faculties cannot train in the noble path, and so lack the three uncontaminated faculties; those with both forms likewise. The statement reflects the treatise's own framework of who can train.

quiz.q: How many faculties do one who has severed wholesome roots and an ordinary being possess?
options: one who has severed roots excepting eight, potentially the rest; an ordinary being nineteen, excepting the final three
one who has severed roots potentially has all of them, while an ordinary being lacks eight, having neither faith and the rest nor the three uncontaminated faculties
both potentially all
both only eight
quiz.why: The treatise says that one who has severed wholesome roots lacks eight, potentially possessing the rest; an ordinary being has nineteen, without the final three. Master Cháng Bǎi: one who has severed roots has no wholesome roots manifesting and they do not continue. Eight means faith and the rest with the three uncontaminated.

quiz.q: How many faculties can an arhat and a non-returner have, and why?
options: nineteen each; the non-returner has severed desire and has no sorrow; the arhat has passed the first two and has no sorrow
twenty-two each, noble ones having all, sorrow included, worrying for beings
non-returner twenty; arhat twenty-one
non-returner eleven; arhat eight
quiz.why: The treatise gives nineteen potentially for both. Master Cháng Bǎi: the non-returner has wholly severed conceptual and innate desire of the desire realm and so has no sorrow; the arhat, having gone beyond the first two uncontaminated faculties, certainly has no desire-realm sorrow. Both counts exclude the two faculties these persons have passed beyond.

quiz.q: What happens to faculties on dying in the desire realm and being reborn there?
options: what is lost and gained are the final three, physical faculties being unchanged for life
all vanish at death, none being gained
one always gains better faculties
in terms of physical faculties: four cases of deficient or complete, superior or inferior; leaving excellent ones and gaining poor ones in evil destinies, and so on
quiz.why: The treatise considers physical faculties, in four cases of deficient and complete and four of inferior and superior. Master Cháng Bǎi: this concerns loss and gain of physical faculties as ripened results in the desire realm, covering good and evil destinies; one may leave the excellent faculties of humans and gods and, in the three evil destinies, gain inferior ones.

quiz.q: How many faculties possess the meaning of an object, and which does not?
options: twenty do, since neither the mind nor life has an object: mind has no fixed object of its own and life is drawn by karma alone, and so only the others are counted
twenty-one do; the life faculty does not, being drawn by karma
all twenty-two do
only the five physical faculties do
quiz.why: The treatise says twenty-one possess it and one does not. Master Cháng Bǎi: the life faculty has no object; it is drawn by past karma, and so cannot be said to have an object. The English has "the meaning of an object" here and "objective meaning" in the next section for the same term.
